<!-- pr-reviewer: afbb25f207e94c2c9ba65539efb013d82ea33508 -->
Review (Opus, read-only): clean

I did not build this PR. I read the diff, #3278, the #3136 diff and the golden writer. I recomputed the golden from the `.cl` text.

**1. Golden diff**
- Moves 1-8 (START, two Rapid, Plunge, the rows at y = 22, 25, 28 and their joins) are byte-identical to main. The old move 9, `Rapid 75000 28000 20000`, is now the last move. So the 9 old moves do not change.
- The header changes from v1 to v2 because `gen_to_cltext` gives v2 to a prismatic path with arcs. `moves=15` is correct: 9 + 6.
- The 6 new moves are one lap of the cutter-centre stadium, one feed and two arcs for each end:
  - `Feed` (75,28) -> (45,28): 3.000 mm off the axis.
  - `Arc` (45,28) -> (42,25) about (45,25), S1: radius 3.000 at both ends, 90 deg -> 180 deg, CCW. Correct.
  - `Arc` (42,25) -> (45,22) about (45,25), S1: radius 3.000, 180 deg -> 270 deg, CCW. Correct.
  - `Feed` (45,22) -> (75,22): 3.000 mm off the axis.
  - `Arc` (75,22) -> (78,25) about (75,25), S1: radius 3.000, 270 deg -> 360 deg, CCW. Correct.
  - `Arc` (78,25) -> (75,28) about (75,25), S1: radius 3.000, 0 deg -> 90 deg, CCW. Correct.
- The allowed cutter-centre offset is 5 - 2 = 3.000 mm. Each new point is exactly 3.000 mm from the axis (45,25) -> (75,25) at the 1 um scale of the file. Maximum overcut: 0.000 mm. Undercut on the wall: 0.000 mm.
- The lap has the same shape as the #3136 golden `slot_wide_channel_rows.cl`: the cap splits at each row offset and at the tip (`slot_lap.rs` `wall_lap`). The rows here are at d = -3, 0, 3, so each cap has two 90 deg arcs.
- The old golden left more than the PR says. On the chord quadrant of each end, the remaining wall is 3 (1 - cos 45 deg) = 0.88 mm, as the PR says. On the other quadrant of each end, no join crosses. At the 45 deg wall point (78.536, 28.536), the nearest cutter centre is (75,28) or (78,25), at 3.576 mm. So 1.58 mm of material stayed on the old path. This is a note only: the conclusion "the old shape was the wrong one" is stronger, not weaker. You can correct the number in the decision file if you push again. It does not block this PR.

**2. The writer**
The golden is the output of `write_golden("slot_dxf_outline.cl", &gen_to_cltext(&path))` (`crates/app/tests/common/mod.rs` lines 121-136 and 234-253). The header format `; HSMW-CL v{version} scale={CL_SCALE}mm moves={n}`, the `Arc ... I.. J.. S1` words and the F words agree with that writer. I found no sign of a hand edit.

**3. The two new asserts**
- The round-end assert needs an arc move about each end centre with both end points at 3 mm +- 1 um. The old golden has no arc move, so this assert fails on the old path. It is not tautological: the centres and the radius are fixed numbers of the fixture, not values that the test reads from the path.
- The containment assert checks each end point of each cutting move against the fixed stadium (3 mm about the fixed axis), and each arc for a centre at an axis end and a radius of at most 3 mm. A full circle of radius 3 or less about an axis end is in the stadium, and the stadium is convex. Thus a line or an arc that passes the checks stays in the stadium. A point 3.001 mm or more off the axis, or an arc of a larger radius, fails it. The old golden passes this assert, which is correct: the old path left material but did not gouge.
- The plunge from z 12 is outside the filter (`from.z < 10`). Its point (45,22) is 3.000 mm off the axis, so this has no effect.
- The stock-simulation assert `gouge_cells == 0` now runs again after the golden compare.

**4. Gates**
- The tree of 4c11e92b7 and the tree of the final head are different only in `docs/decisions/3278-slot-dxf-golden.md` (`git diff --stat 4c11e92b7 afbb25f20`). So the 690-step quick gate applies to all the code and test text of the final head. The body says that the quick gate ran "without the outline-containment assert", but 4c11e92b7 contains that assert. Probably the gate ran on the tree before the commit. The touched binary `slot_dxf_sketch` ran 4/4 on the final head, and that covers the assert.
- No generator code changes. Only `slot_dxf_sketch.rs` reads this golden (`git grep`). I agree that the heavy lanes are not necessary.
- Main moved from the merge base 5c8340b81 to 03e05a649. The new main commits change `machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`, `descent_xy.rs` and `lead_ext.rs`, not `slots.rs` or `slot_lap.rs`. The trial merge is clean (`git merge-tree`). The post-merge run 44983843143 on 03e05a649 is red only on this one test. I think this is enough. As a low-cost check before the merge, the merging session can run `cargo xtask gate test a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size --crate camcraft-app --binary slot_dxf_sketch --exact` on the merge with 03e05a649. This is a recommendation, not a blocker.

**5. Decision file**
`docs/decisions/3278-slot-dxf-golden.md` has the `## #N - <title>` heading and the what, why, dropped and cost parts, as `docs/decisions/README.md` specifies. The format is correct. One line in it is long (the "0.88 mm" line), and the number is low (see 1).

**6. Other checks**
- `Fixes #3278` is in the body. `Changelog: none` is correct for a golden-only change.
- No process file changes. No snapshot PNG changes.

Blockers: none.

Coordinator: this PR fixes a red `main` (#3278, P2). The review that this merge relies on is comment 7074311345 (Opus, read-only, clean, head afbb25f20). The reviewer recomputed each new move of the golden: 0.000 mm overcut and 0.000 mm undercut. The quick gate (690 steps, 0 failed) covers the test code of this head, and `slot_dxf_sketch` ran 4 of 4 on this head. No generator code changes. The trial merge with the current `main` is clean. I flag it ready and merge it on head afbb25f20. Nothing is pushed after this flag.
